title: Dungeon Dive Hobbycast - Episode 2: Ten Things I Look for in a Great Dungeon Crawl or Adventure Game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hwi-jokx7aI

Fresh off ranking his top 50, Daniel (@dungeondive) works backwards from the list to the criteria — ten qualities he would specify if he were commissioning a dungeon crawl built to order. Each one is checked against the games that actually made his top ten, which turns the episode into a working explanation of that list rather than a wish list in the abstract.

The ten, unordered: an extensive bestiary where monsters genuinely differ; a **character** campaign over a narrative one — persistent heroes rather than a novel in chapters; fast-paced combat that resolves in a few dice rather than a war of attrition; non-combat encounters; things to do *outside* the dungeon, so the dungeon is part of the game and not all of it; loot carrying a line of lore rather than a bigger number; stat checks that make a character's non-combat build matter; co-op and solo over one-versus-many, scaling to heroes rather than players; a sense of exploration; and lots of randomness, so plans get thrown out.

*Warhammer Quest*, *Shadows of Brimstone*, *Sleeping Gods*, *Machina Arcana*, *Secrets of the Lost Tomb* and *HEXplore It* recur throughout. He concedes one top-ten game satisfies almost none of these and earns its place on fun alone.

----

Which of the ten would you drop from your own list — and what would you put in its place?
